name: Soil Moisture
description: The dampness or dryness of the soil significantly impacts the robot's traction and speed, particularly on the grass path (Path 2).  Drier soil increases friction on the grass, slowing the robot and creating variable travel times. Higher likelihood due to direct physical impact and relatively consistent spatial variation across a field.

name: Grass Density & Height
description: The density and height of the grass on Path 2 directly affects the robot's ability to navigate. Taller, denser grass slows the robot more significantly than short, sparse grass. Variable heights and densities introduce multimodal travel times. High likelihood as it's the primary surface of Path 2.

name: Time of Day (Sunlight & Temperature)
description: Solar radiation intensity and temperature affect the surface temperature of both paths, leading to differences in friction. Path 2 (grass) will heat up faster and retain heat longer than the relatively cooler Path 1 (track).  These temperature changes affect traction and robot speed. High likelihood due to the diurnal cycle.

name: Rainfall/Recent Rain
description: Recent rainfall saturates the grass on Path 2, drastically reducing traction and increasing travel time. Path 1, being a hard-surface track, is less affected. This creates a highly variable travel time response. Moderate likelihood due to the localized impact of weather events.

name: Robot Wheel Slip
description: The amount of wheel slip the robot experiences affects travel time. Variations in wheel slip depend on surface conditions and robot speed.  This contributes to travel time variability. Moderate likelihood - it's an inherent consequence of traversing uneven terrain.

name: Crop Row Spacing
description: The distance between crop rows on Path 2 directly affects the robot's ability to maneuver and the time it takes to navigate around them. Changes in spacing influence travel time, particularly at corners or turns. Moderate likelihood due to Path 2’s constrained environment.

name: Slope/Terrain Variation
description: Even minor changes in slope (elevation differences) affect the robot's speed and traction, creating variations in travel time. This is more pronounced on Path 2. Moderate likelihood – fields are rarely perfectly flat.

name: Wind Speed & Direction
description: Wind resistance can impact the robot's speed, especially during turns or when traversing open areas.  This is more pronounced on open paths and could affect the robot's stability.  Low likelihood – typically a small factor compared to traction.

name: Robot Battery Level
description: As battery level decreases, robot speed can be reduced, leading to longer travel times. Low likelihood – a controlled aspect of operation but can be a confounding factor.

name: Path Surface Obstacles (Rocks, Debris)
description: Small rocks, fallen leaves, or other debris on either path will cause the robot to slow down or even stop, leading to variable travel times. Low likelihood – dependent on field maintenance.

name: Crop Type
description: The specific type of crop in the field affects the density and height of the grass along Path 2, and potentially the surface properties of Path 1 if the track is adjacent to the crop row. Low likelihood – primarily impacts grass density.

name: Maintenance Operations (Human Activity)
description: Human workers or equipment operating in the field could temporarily block paths or introduce variations in surface conditions. Very Low likelihood – unpredictable, but potentially impactful.

name: Robot Wheel Wear
description: Wear on the robot's wheels can affect traction and speed, contributing to variations in travel time. Very Low likelihood - cumulative effect.

name: Lighting Conditions (Cloud Cover)
description: Changes in cloud cover can affect the amount of sunlight reaching the robot, potentially influencing surface temperatures and thus traction. Very Low likelihood - related to Time of Day.

name: Field Slope Orientation
description: The direction of the slope on the field – whether it's oriented north-south, east-west – can affect how sunlight and wind patterns influence temperature and moisture on the paths. Very Low likelihood - a long-term spatial characteristic.
